<STRUCT_0001>
It seems that this is the accepted definition. An alternative, which lends
itself more readily to generalizations beyond the <ACCENT_0001>tale site of a scheme,
would have been to define constructible sheaves by starting with
<MATH_0001>, <MATH_0002>, and <MATH_0003>
where <MATH_0004> runs over all quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects
of <MATH_0005>, and then take the smallest full subcategory of
<MATH_0006>, <MATH_0007>, and
<MATH_0008> containing these
and closed under finite limits and colimits. It follows from
Lemma <REF_0001>
and
Lemmas <REF_0002>,
<REF_0003>, and
<REF_0004>
that this produces the same category if <MATH_0009> is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. In general this does not produce the same
category however.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
A disjoint union decomposition <MATH_0010> of a scheme by
locally closed subschemes will be called a <TEXTITOPEN_0001>partition<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> of <MATH_0011>
(compare with Topology, Section <REF_0005>).

Let <MATH_0001> be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let <MATH_0002>
be a sheaf of sets on <MATH_0003>. The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0004> is constructible,
<STRUCT_0003> there exists an open covering <MATH_0005> such that
<MATH_0006> is constructible, and
<STRUCT_0004> there exists a partition <MATH_0007> by constructible
locally closed subschemes such that <MATH_0008> is finite
locally constant.
<STRUCT_0005>
A similar statement holds for abelian sheaves and sheaves of
<MATH_0009>-modules if <MATH_0010> is Noetherian.

It is clear that (1) implies (2).

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assume (2). For every <MATH_0001> we can find an <MATH_0002> and an affine open
neighbourhood <MATH_0003> of <MATH_0004>. Hence we can find a finite
affine open covering <MATH_0005> such that for each <MATH_0006> there
exists a finite decomposition <MATH_0007> by locally closed
constructible subsets such that <MATH_0008> is finite
locally constant. By Topology, Lemma
<REF_0001>
each <MATH_0009> is constructible as a subset of <MATH_0010>.
By Topology, Lemma
<REF_0002>
we can find a finite stratification <MATH_0011> with constructible
locally closed strata such that each
<MATH_0012> is a union of <MATH_0013>. Thus (3) holds.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Assume (3) holds. Let <MATH_0014> be an affine open.
Then <MATH_0015> is a constructible locally closed subset of <MATH_0016>
(for example by Properties, Lemma <REF_0003>)
and <MATH_0017> is a partition of <MATH_0018> as in
Definition <REF_0004>. Thus (1) holds.

Let <MATH_0001> be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let <MATH_0002> be a sheaf of sets, abelian groups,
<MATH_0003>-modules (with <MATH_0004> Noetherian) on <MATH_0005>.
If there exist constructible locally closed subschemes <MATH_0006>
such that (a) <MATH_0007> and (b) <MATH_0008> is
constructible, then <MATH_0009> is constructible.

First, we can assume the covering is finite as <MATH_0001> is quasi-compact
in the spectral topology
(Topology, Lemma <REF_0001>
and
Properties, Lemma
<REF_0002>).
Observe that each <MATH_0002> is a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
scheme in its own right (because it is constructible in <MATH_0003>; details omitted).
Thus we can find a finite partition <MATH_0004> into
locally closed constructible parts of <MATH_0005> such that
<MATH_0006> is finite locally constant
(Lemma <REF_0003>).
By Topology, Lemma <REF_0004>
we see that <MATH_0007> is a constructible locally closed subscheme of <MATH_0008>.
Then we can apply Topology, Lemma
<REF_0005>
to <MATH_0009> to find the desired partition of <MATH_0010>.
